source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter I, §1 Some Simple Mates, Example 4

steps.title: The easiest mate of all
steps.source: As the Queen combines the power of the Rook and the Bishop, it is the easiest mate of all and should always be accomplished in under ten moves.

narration.say: The queen combines the power of the rook and the bishop.
That makes this the easiest mate of all. It should always take fewer than ten moves.

steps.title: Start with the queen
steps.source: A good way to begin is to make the first move with the Queen, trying to limit the Black King's mobility as much as possible.

narration.say: A good start is a queen move that limits the black king as much as possible.
King to d2. Look: the black king has only one square left.
King to e3. Black to f5.
Queen to d6. Black to g5.
Queen to e6. Black runs to the edge, on h4.
The black king is on the h-file. Find a quiet queen move that keeps him trapped there.

exercise.prompt: A quiet queen move that locks the king on the edge.

feedback.Qh6: Check, but the king escapes to g4. No hurry: take squares away instead.
feedback.*: Put the queen on the g-file, a knight's jump away from the king.

exercise.hint: The queen goes one file away from the king, on the g-file.
exercise.success: Right: 6. Qg6. The black king can only go to h3.

steps.title: Your turn: bring the king
steps.source: In each case the co-operation of the King is needed.

narration.say: The queen alone cannot mate. The white king must come closer. Your move.

exercise.prompt: Bring the white king closer. Watch out for stalemate.

feedback.*: Step the king towards the black king, to f3.

exercise.hint: The king goes diagonally towards the black king.
exercise.success: 7. Kf3. Black has to move, and goes to h2.

narration.say: The queen mates next move. Find it.

exercise.prompt: White to move and give checkmate in one.

feedback.*: Not mate. The queen should go right next to the black king, protected by your king.

exercise.hint: The queen lands next to the black king, defended by the white king.

steps.title: The three elementary endings
steps.source: These are the three elementary endings and in all of these the principle is the same. In each case the co-operation of the King is needed. In order to force a mate without the aid of the King, at least two Rooks are required.

narration.say: Rook, two bishops, queen: these are the three elementary endings.
The principle is always the same: drive the enemy king to the edge of the board.
And in each case the king must help. Without the king, you need at least two rooks to force mate.
